title: Rails queries: indexes, batching, and bounded reports
outcome: Choose SQL work, Ruby work, and batching with attention to memory and business semantics.
useCase: Exports, list screens, and repair jobs.
drawbacks: Batching and snapshot semantics can change the meaning of a report.
cue: Count rows, objects, and queries separately.

trace.title: Scoped relation
trace.detail: A report can be correct on ten rows and fail on a million. Ask how many rows are loaded, how many model objects are built, how many queries run, and whether the order matters.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Request scope → SQL predicate/order → database plan → limited rows/batches → Ruby transformation → output. Measure rows, query count, and memory at separate points.

For an export, decide what happens when tickets change while it runs. A transaction snapshot may give stability but can be expensive over a long job; a materialized export scope is another tradeoff.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: to_a before filtering moves potentially huge work into Ruby memory. Per-row association reads create N+1. A batch loop that changes its own selection criteria needs a progress rule.
